Bob works in the number factory. One day when Bob is working his boss comes to visit him and gives him a strange assignment, "Bob I need you to make me a nine without using any numbers" Bob thinks long and hard about how to do this and eventually goes outside and hangs a star on three trees. Near the end of the day his boss comes to him and asks him what he's done and Bob says, "Tree plus tree plus tree equals nine" His boss is very pleased and lets him go home early.

The next day Bob's boss comes back into his office with a new assignment, "I need you to make 99 without using any numbers" Once again Bob thinks about what to do and eventually goes outside and splashes mud on the tree trees from yesterday. Near the end of the day his boss comes to him and asks him what he's done and Bob says,
"Dirty tree plus dirty tree plus dirty tree equals 99" Once again his boss is very pleased and lets him go home early.

The next day Bob's boss comes back into his office with a yet another assignment, "I need you to make 100 without using any numbers" This one is especially tricky but eventually Bob goes outside and visits the trees from before with his dog. Near the end of the day his boss comes to him and asks him what he's done and Bob says,
"Dirty tree and a turd plus dirty tree and a turd plus dirty tree and a turd equals 100".

I haven't been in your situation since I used to play Dota in a competitive level, but I wanted to ask you: why are you losing your games? Is it because you lose your lane, or you can't close a game that was in your favor?
Well you can't always win. You win some, you lose some. Some things are out of your control.
Some things are out of control, but you will win more if you play well and less if you play badly.

Do you know what specifically you're having problems with?

One of the most important things I learned was to understand your role. If you're the tank, you should engage and soak damage if you know you have follow-up. Assassins should be able to 100-0 someone on the enemy team up to a certain point. If you're the tank/bruiser of the team, peel the enemy off your main damage dealers. Dying is fine as long as you can keep the ADC alive long enough for them to be relevant in the fight. It's not always about KD.
Also, following up on knowing your role, what helped me was maining a role until I understood my importance in team fights.

The thing that helps me the most with getting over a hump of losing or when I lose motivation to play is usually to just focus on what I can be improving on rather than winning. Am i having trouble CS'ing for whatever reason? Time to focus on that for the next few days. Am i just sucking all the time in lane? Ok so i need to play safer and pick better match ups. My point is the whole time when im focusing on my play im never focusing on winning all that hard, dont get me wrong winning is a fucking great feeling, but if you just play winning will just come with the game. Just start setting goals for yourself and when you accomplish them, great! Now move onto the next one! Sorry if this doesnt really help with the motivation side of things, but you can also just stop playing if you feel like the game isnt for you and its making you feel exhausted when you play! Hey man, fellow Bronzie here. Throughout this season I climbed out of Bronze 5, and made it to Bronze 2. Here are some of the things I've done, and hopefully can help you.

  • Learn to play passively. If you fall behind, don't initiate engages, and only take CS that the enemy can't contest, and trade heavily with you over. (IE: Don't walk through the minion wave to cs when the enemy Leona has all her CDs up.)
  • Always have in mind what your short-term goal is. This doesn't matter too much in laning phase, as it's always the same, but it comes into play in the midgame. I've always found that Bronze players (myself included) run around like chickens with their heads cut off in the midgame, pushing random lanes, applying pressure when they shouldn't be, not applying pressure when the should, etc.. For example if your 25 minutes into the game, and dragon is spawning in 1:30, that's your main goal at the time, and you should take steps to be able to secure that easier. This means, get wards and sweepers around the pit, push out the toplane, and then do your best not to get caught until dragon spawns.
  • Ward. Just do it. I was always told to ward more and I always said, 'yeah yeah I know," but then once I got into game I just, stopped.
  • Use the mute button. If someones pissing you off, just mute them. Helps you avoid tilting or making bad plays because you're more focused on the flamer than the game at hand.

Lastly, if you're on NA and you wanna play sometime, send me a PM :)

I started as Bronze as well and my goal was always Gold to get those juicy free skins at the end of every season. The thing that helped me the most was keeping logs. After each ranked game, win or lose, 20-0 or 0-20, I would write down all the mistakes that I remembered making. After a while I notice patterns in things I keep doing wrong every game, which I then tried to stop repeating.

For me it was things like trading kills 1 for 1 when I was already ahead, overstaying after a kill or turret to get more cs or an inhib and then dying to reinforcements rather than just taking the small victory and backing out, pushing too far into enemy territory without wards, buying wards and forgetting to place them, placing wards but forgetting to watch the minimap.

My mechanics didn't get any better between bronze to gold, just fixing a number of small decision making mistakes one by one added up to make a big difference in my ability to win games. imaqtpie always says LoL is a decision making game, and I agree with that.
